title: 心理情報とキャリアデザイン
subtitle: Career Desing for Psychology and Information Design
teachers:
KAWASHIMA Tomoya
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: This department aims to cultivate professionals who can apply the knowledge and skills acquired at university with a broad perspective toward society, creating information design that enriches people's lives. Therefore, this course aims to have students consider how psychology can be applied in society through lectures and exercises. Specifically, students will tackle challenges presented by partner companies, practicing psychology-based information design through these projects.
advice:
This subject is eligible for the course credit system.

This course combines lectures by department faculty with practical information design exercises conducted through team activities.
In the lectures, students will learn how psychology contributes to society through examples of faculty members' actual collaborative research with companies and case studies of department graduates.
In the practical exercises, partner companies will present information design challenges. Students will work in teams to devise solutions and propose them to the companies.
　
This provides a valuable opportunity to apply psychological knowledge to meet corporate needs. Students are encouraged to actively participate in team activities and other efforts to ensure their ideas are adopted by the companies.

              This department aims to cultivate professionals who can apply the knowledge and skills acquired at university with a broad perspective toward society, creating information design that enriches people's lives. Therefore, this course aims to have students consider how psychology can be applied in society through lectures and exercises. Specifically, students will tackle challenges presented by partner companies, practicing psychology-based information design through these projects.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This subject is eligible for the course credit system.

This course combines lectures by department faculty with practical information design exercises conducted through team activities.
In the lectures, students will learn how psychology contributes to society through examples of faculty members' actual collaborative research with companies and case studies of department graduates.
In the practical exercises, partner companies will present information design challenges. Students will work in teams to devise solutions and propose them to the companies.
　
This provides a valuable opportunity to apply psychological knowledge to meet corporate needs. Students are encouraged to actively participate in team activities and other efforts to ensure their ideas are adopted by the companies.
